records.issue_text: `app/controllers/embed_controller.rb:15`: Unknown-URL requests enqueue jobs before worker-side throttling, allowing clients with spoofed Referer headers to flood the Sidekiq queue with no-op jobs
records.rationale: Verifiable in the diff: embed_controller.rb's `best` action calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` for any embed_url not found in TopicEmbed, before any rate limiting. The throttle ($redis setnx 60s) only exists inside TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?, which runs on the worker after the job is already enqueued, and `no_throttle` is even set for staff users via the job args. The referer/host check (ensure_embeddable) requires only a matching Referer header, which a non-browser client can set freely. So a client can flood the Sidekiq queue with no-op jobs. records.issue_text: `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:35`: Feed-provided HTML is imported using `raw_html` without sanitization, allowing malicious scripts or event handlers to execute under the forum's origin
records.rationale: Verified: poll_feed.rb takes `i.content` from the feed and passes to TopicEmbed.import, which creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`; Post#cook then does `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, bypassing the sanitizing cooking pipeline. The embed view renders `raw post.cooked`, so injected scripts/handlers from the feed would execute under the forum's origin. This is a genuine, verifiable security defect introduced by this diff.

records.issue_text: `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:40-44`: The spec expects direct `TopicRetriever` invocation even though the controller now uses `Jobs.enqueue`, causing test failure and leaving asynchronous behavior untested
records.rationale: The controller's `best` action calls `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: current_user.try(:id), embed_url: embed_url)` (embed_controller.rb), but the spec at spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb stubs `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)` and `retriever.expects(:retrieve)`, which the controller never invokes directly — so the spec's expectations will not be met and the test fails. Both the controller and spec are in this diff, so the mismatch is directly verifiable.
